# Model: the plan P has three load-bearing claims:
#   G1: students can relieve the security shortage (competence)
#   G2: the participants are the financially needy (economic goal)
#   F : the plan can be carried out for ALL non-returning students (funding/feasibility)
# An option "can question" the plan iff it entails the negation of at least one claim.
# The mapping option -> claims it undermines is a hand-encoded semantic judgment,
# so this check is a model of the argument, not a proof about natural language.
from itertools import product

claims = ["G1_competence", "G2_needy", "F_feasible_for_all"]

# Each option is encoded as the set of claims it contradicts.
# A: not all non-returners are poor            -> undermines G2
# B: students are hardly competent for duty    -> undermines G1
# C: limited funds, many students              -> undermines F
# D: most signed up for English classes        -> classes are part-time/compatible with
#    work; it says nothing about need, competence, or funding -> undermines nothing
#    (the "busy schedule" reading is an extra assumption not entailed by the option)
options = {
    "A": {"G2_needy"},
    "B": {"G1_competence"},
    "C": {"F_feasible_for_all"},
    "D": set(),
}

# Enumerate all truth assignments to the claims; the plan is "sound" only if all three hold.
def plan_sound(w):
    return all(w[c] for c in claims)

results = {}
for name, undermines in options.items():
    # Worlds consistent with the option: every undermined claim is false.
    worlds = []
    for vals in product([True, False], repeat=len(claims)):
        w = dict(zip(claims, vals))
        if all(not w[c] for c in undermines):
            worlds.append(w)
    # The option questions the plan if it rules out soundness in every consistent world.
    questions = all(not plan_sound(w) for w in worlds)
    results[name] = questions
    print(name, "questions plan:", questions, "| consistent worlds:", len(worlds))

cannot_question = [k for k, v in results.items() if not v]
print("Options that cannot question the plan:", cannot_question)

submitted = "D"
if cannot_question == [submitted]:
    print("CHECK PASS (under the encoded model; the mapping is a semantic judgment)")
else:
    print("CHECK FAIL")
